challenges.title: Cycle detection never stops
challenges.brief: Walking a circular list with a null check loops forever.
challenges.error: Timeout — no output
challenges.explain: A cycle has no null to stop on. Floyd's slow/fast pointers detect it in O(n) time and O(1) space.
hints: A null check cannot detect a loop.
Two pointers at different speeds must meet inside a cycle.

challenges.title: Reusing a consumed stream
challenges.brief: The second terminal operation throws IllegalStateException.
challenges.actual: Exception in thread "main" java.lang.IllegalStateException: stream has already been operated upon or closed
challenges.error: IllegalStateException: stream has already been operated upon or closed
challenges.explain: A stream is a one-shot pipeline. Create a fresh stream from the collection for each terminal operation.
hints: A stream cannot be consumed twice.

challenges.title: Unordered groupingBy
challenges.brief: The report prints groups in an unpredictable order.
challenges.error: No exception — HashMap ordering is unspecified.
challenges.explain: The two-argument groupingBy uses a HashMap. Supplying TreeMap::new as the map factory sorts the keys.
hints: Which Map does groupingBy create by default?

challenges.title: Shared list in a parallel stream
challenges.brief: Adding to an ArrayList inside parallel() loses elements.
challenges.error: No exception — a data race silently drops updates.
challenges.explain: ArrayList is not thread-safe, and forEach runs on several threads. Use a collector or a reduction instead of mutating shared state.

challenges.title: Reader never closed
challenges.brief: The file handle leaks because the reader is not closed.
challenges.error: No exception locally — leaks file descriptors under load
challenges.explain: try-with-resources closes the reader even if an exception is thrown, and also deletes the temporary file here.

challenges.title: Counting lines
challenges.brief: The line count is one short because the last line has no trailing newline.
challenges.error: No exception — the loop only counts newline characters.
challenges.explain: readLine returns null only after the final line, with or without a trailing newline. Files.readAllLines counts them for you.
hints: readLine returns each line, then null.

challenges.title: Raw type ClassCastException
challenges.brief: A raw List accepts a String and the cast to Integer fails at runtime.
challenges.actual: Exception in thread "main" java.lang.ClassCastException: class java.lang.String cannot be cast to class java.lang.Integer
challenges.error: ClassCastException: String cannot be cast to Integer
challenges.explain: Raw types disable the compiler's checks, moving the failure to runtime. Generics make the wrong type a compile error instead.
hints: What type does the list really hold?

challenges.title: Comparing type parameters
challenges.brief: A generic max method does not compile because T has no ordering.
challenges.actual: javac: bad operand types for binary operator '>'
challenges.error: error: bad operand types for binary operator '>'
challenges.explain: Operators like > only work on primitives. A Comparable bound gives the type a compareTo method.

challenges.title: Lost updates
challenges.brief: Four threads increment a plain int and the total is too low.
challenges.error: No exception — counter++ is read-modify-write and races.
challenges.explain: counter++ is three steps: read, add, write. Another thread can interleave between them. AtomicInteger makes it one atomic operation.
hints: How many steps are in counter++?
Use an atomic type or synchronized.

challenges.title: Deadlock from lock order
challenges.brief: Two threads take the same two locks in opposite order and hang.
challenges.error: Timeout — no output
challenges.explain: Deadlock needs a circular wait. If every thread acquires locks in the same global order, the cycle cannot form.

challenges.title: Executor never shut down
challenges.brief: The program hangs after printing because the pool's threads are non-daemon.
challenges.error: Timeout after the expected output
challenges.explain: Pool threads keep the JVM alive. shutdown() lets queued work finish and then terminates the workers.
hints: Which threads keep the JVM running?
Call shutdown in a finally block.

challenges.title: Ignoring a String result
challenges.brief: replace() returns a new string, so the original is unchanged.
challenges.error: No exception — the returned value is discarded.
challenges.explain: String is immutable; every transforming method returns a new instance. Assign the result if you want to keep it.

challenges.title: while loop without progress
challenges.brief: The while loop never increments i, so the program hangs.
challenges.error: Timeout — no output
challenges.explain: Every loop body must move the loop variable toward the exit condition. A for loop keeps the update visible in the header.

challenges.title: Unboxing a null Integer
challenges.brief: A nullable Integer is assigned to int and throws NullPointerException.
challenges.error: NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "java.lang.Integer.intValue()" because "boxed" is null
challenges.explain: Assigning an Integer to an int triggers intValue(), which throws on null. Check for null before unboxing.

challenges.title: Reading when input is empty
challenges.brief: nextInt on empty input throws NoSuchElementException.
challenges.error: NoSuchElementException
challenges.explain: nextInt throws when no token is available. hasNextInt lets you handle empty or malformed input gracefully.
hints: What happens when there is no token?

challenges.title: Aliasing an array
challenges.brief: Copying an array reference shares the same data, so both arrays change.
challenges.error: No exception — two references point at one array.
challenges.explain: Assignment copies the reference, not the elements. Arrays.copyOf allocates a new backing array.
hints: Are original and copy the same object?

challenges.title: Search aborts on the first mismatch
challenges.brief: Linear search returns -1 as soon as the first element is not the key.
challenges.error: No exception — an early return skips the rest of the array.
challenges.explain: Return only when you find the key. Falling out of the loop means the key is absent.
hints: Should a mismatch end the search?

challenges.title: Uninitialized rows
challenges.brief: A jagged array with null rows throws NullPointerException on assignment.
challenges.error: NullPointerException: Cannot store to int array because "m[0]" is null
challenges.explain: new int[3][] allocates only the row slots. Each row must be allocated separately unless you use new int[3][2].

challenges.title: Missing toString
challenges.brief: Printing an object shows a hash code instead of its fields.
challenges.error: No exception — Object.toString is inherited.
challenges.explain: The default toString is class name plus identity hash. Override it to make logs and test output readable.
hints: Where does the @hash value come from?

challenges.title: Static counter shared by all instances
challenges.brief: Two counters share one static total, so both print 2.
challenges.error: No exception — static state belongs to the class, not the instance.
challenges.explain: One static field exists per class. Remove static when each object needs its own copy.
hints: How many copies of a static field exist?
Make the field an instance field.

challenges.title: Unboxing a missing key
challenges.brief: map.get on an absent key returns null, and assigning it to int throws.
challenges.error: NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "java.lang.Integer.intValue()" because the return value of "Map.get(Object)" is null
challenges.explain: get returns null for a missing key. getOrDefault supplies a fallback and avoids the unboxing NPE.
hints: What does get return when the key is absent?

challenges.title: Stack used as a queue
challenges.brief: A queue built on push/pop returns items in LIFO order.
challenges.error: No exception — the wrong end is used.
challenges.explain: push/pop operate on the head, which makes a stack. A queue adds at the tail and removes from the head.

challenges.title: Head removal not reflected
challenges.brief: Removing the first node does not update the caller's head reference.
challenges.error: No exception — the list still points at the removed node.
challenges.explain: Removing the head means moving the head pointer itself; skipping a middle node only rewires next.
hints: Which node should become the new head?

challenges.title: Optional.get on an empty value
challenges.brief: get() on an empty Optional throws instead of returning a default.
challenges.actual: Exception in thread "main" java.util.NoSuchElementException: No value present
challenges.error: NoSuchElementException: No value present
challenges.explain: get() is the one method that defeats Optional's purpose. orElse, orElseGet or ifPresent handle absence explicitly.

challenges.title: Calling a subclass method through a parent type
challenges.brief: The parent reference cannot call a method that exists only on the subclass.
challenges.actual: javac: cannot find symbol: method speak()
challenges.error: error: cannot find symbol — method speak()
challenges.explain: The compiler uses the declared type, so the method must exist on Animal. Overriding gives Dog its own behaviour while the call stays polymorphic.
hints: Which type does the compiler check?
Declare the method on the parent.
